channel.title: Treasure Coast Today
channel.description: Local news for Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties, Florida.

item.title: North Palm Beach celebrates Fourth of July with fireworks and pool party at country club
item.description: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.

item.title: Juno Beach residents demand fence at JB-7 beach access as trespassing complaints rise
item.description: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.

item.title: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk Facebook comments
item.description: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year for Facebook comment.

item.title: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to win 2026 All-America City Award
item.description: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League and was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.

item.title: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida in National Independence Day Parade
item.description: The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade and will represent the entire state of Florida.

item.title: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
item.description: For the third year in a row, the School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state, with 143 district-operated schools rated A or B.

item.title: Hobe Sound community raises funds for man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
item.description: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside the couple's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.

item.title: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem denies reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
item.description: Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure.

item.title: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire days before her birthday
item.description: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home that investigators believe was caused by an electrical issue. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed the couple's belongings.

item.description: Colony Condos residents say beachgoers using the JB-7 public walkway have been cutting through private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023. A replacement could cost the town thousands of dollars.

item.title: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
item.description: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved giving 7 acres of land to FDOT for a partial Turnpike interchange as the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project continues. The interchange aims to fill a significant gap between Turnpike entrances in the city.

item.title: California company proposes elevated self-driving network linking West Palm Beach to airport
item.description: Glydways will present to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday a proposal for autonomous electric vehicles on an elevated guideway connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The trip could take less than 10 minutes.

item.title: Martin County maritime teams prepare for hundreds of Fourth of July boaters
item.description: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby this weekend as hundreds of boaters celebrate the Fourth of July. Lt. Brett Harry urges boaters to keep eyes on the water and have a designated driver.
